# Base image for the build
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments
# This prevents issues with shared memory mechanisms (vader) and high-speed interconnects (openib)
# not typically available in standard container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib

# Install build dependencies, MPI, and required tools
# ca-certificates is included for secure network operations (e.g., git, wget)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \    
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create a build directory and compile all dependencies and the application from source
# This is done in a single RUN layer to optimize image size by allowing for cleanup of build artifacts.
RUN mkdir -p /build && cd /build && \
    # 1. Build METIS 4.0.3
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We download, build, and manually install it.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis-4.0.3.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make OPTFLAGS='-O3 -fPIC -Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration' && \
    mkdir -p /usr/local/metis/include /usr/local/metis/lib && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/metis/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/metis/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    # 2. Build Hypre 2.28.0
    # This is a dependency for MFEM. We configure with big-int support and without Fortran.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre-2.28.0.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local/hypre --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    cd /build && \
    # 3. Build MFEM 4.7
    # This is the core finite element library dependency for Laghos.
    # METIS_INC and METIS_LIB are explicitly set to provide the precise header and library paths,
    # ensuring MFEM's generated config is correct for the downstream Laghos build.
    wget --no-check-certificate https://github.com/mfem/mfem/archive/refs/tags/v4.7.tar.gz -O mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf mfem-4.7.tar.gz && \
    cd mfem-4.7 && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local/hypre METIS_INC='-I/usr/local/metis/include' METIS_LIB='-L/usr/local/metis/lib -lmetis' CXX=mpicxx && \
    cd /build && \
    # 4. Build Laghos
    # The final application build. It links against the previously built MFEM library.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem-4.7 && \
    # 5. Install the executable
    # Copy the final binary to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # 6. Prepare the runtime directory and copy data files
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp data/* /app/ && \
    # 7. Cleanup build artifacts
    # Remove the entire build directory to reduce the final image size.
    cd / && rm -rf /build

# Set the default working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

#
# This manifest defines a Flux Framework MiniCluster to run a Laghos HPC experiment.
# It is configured for a single-node CPU environment on Kubernetes, such as an AWS EC2 instance.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deployment will occur in the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods that form the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to constrain the experiment to a single Kubernetes node.
  size: 1

  # Total number of MPI tasks (ranks) to run for the job.
  # This will schedule 4 Laghos processes on the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # Instructs the Flux Operator not to delete the job pods upon completion.
  # This is crucial for debugging and inspecting results and logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging configuration for the Flux job.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict logging; the job will fail on any logging errors.
    strict: true

  # Defines the pod specification for the MiniCluster.
  # There is only one container definition, which will be used for all pods.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command to be executed by the Flux scheduler.
      # The Flux Operator automatically prepends `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # This command runs the Laghos proxy application with a specific mesh problem.
      # It assumes 'cube_311_hex.mesh' is in the container's working directory.
      command: laghos -p 0 -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # Per instructions, the main application container must not be a launcher.
      # The operator will designate the first pod (pod-0) as the lead broker by default.
      launcher: false

import math
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal
import json

def evaluate_laghos_run(
    total_elements: int,
    total_ranks: int,
    nodes_used: int,
    cores_per_node: int,
    memory_gb_per_node: int,
    threading_hint: int,
    current_fom: float,
    threshold: float = 0.90,
    ideal_fom_per_core: float = 1.5e6,
    efficiency_sweet_spot: float = 35000.0,
    elements_per_gb: float = 1.0e6,
    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.90
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Evaluates a Laghos run and provides a high-level decision and strategic hint.

    This function acts as a "diagnostician" by analyzing the performance of a
    completed Laghos run against a theoretical model. It identifies the most
    likely bottleneck (memory, poor scaling, or hardware underutilization) and
    returns a machine-readable strategic hint for what to try next.

    Args:
        total_elements (int): The total number of mesh elements in the simulation.
        total_ranks (int): The total number of MPI tasks used for the run.
        nodes_used (int): The number of compute nodes used for the run.
        cores_per_node (int): The number of physical CPU cores on a single compute node.
        memory_gb_per_node (int): The total system RAM in Gigabytes on a single compute node.
        threading_hint (int): Specifies the SMT/Hyper-Threading level to assume (e.g., 1 for no SMT, 2 for SMT).
        current_fom (float): The measured performance from the run, typically in FOM/second.
        threshold (float): The performance goal, as a fraction of the theoretical maximum (default 0.90).
        ideal_fom_per_core (float): A tuning constant for the max FOM of a single core (default 1.5e6 FOM/sec).
        efficiency_sweet_spot (float): A tuning constant for elements/rank needed for ~76% efficiency (default 35,000).
        elements_per_gb (float): A tuning constant for the memory model (elements per GB of RAM, default 1.0e6).
        memory_safety_factor (float): A safety margin for memory usage (default 0.90).

    Returns:
        (dict): A dictionary containing 'decision', 'reason', 'strategy_hint', and 'metrics'.
    """
    if total_ranks == 0:
        return {"decision": "RETRY", "reason": "The number of tasks cannot be zero.", "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS"}

    # --- Calculate Theoretical Performance and Ratios ---
    elements_per_rank = total_elements / total_ranks
    max_cores_on_node = cores_per_node * threading_hint
    cores_per_rank = max_cores_on_node // total_ranks if nodes_used == 1 else cores_per_node
    total_cores_used = total_ranks * cores_per_rank
    
    scaling_efficiency = math.tanh(elements_per_rank / efficiency_sweet_spot)
    effective_fom_per_core = ideal_fom_per_core * scaling_efficiency
    theoretical_max_fom = effective_fom_per_core * total_cores_used

    performance_ratio = 0.0
    if theoretical_max_fom > 1e-9:
        performance_ratio = current_fom / theoretical_max_fom

    estimated_memory_gb = total_elements / elements_per_gb
    memory_utilization = estimated_memory_gb / (memory_gb_per_node * nodes_used) if nodes_used > 0 else 0
    
    metrics = {
        "performance_ratio": round(performance_ratio, 3),
        "scaling_efficiency": round(scaling_efficiency, 3),
        "memory_utilization": round(memory_utilization, 3),
        "elements_per_rank": int(elements_per_rank),
        "theoretical_max_fom_per_sec": f"{theoretical_max_fom:.2e}"
    }

    # --- Decision Logic based on prioritized bottlenecks ---
    
    if performance_ratio >= threshold:
        return {
            "decision": "STOP",
            "reason": f"Optimization goal reached. Current performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of the theoretical maximum, meeting the {threshold:.1%} threshold.",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if memory_utilization >= memory_safety_factor:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Memory utilization is critically high at {memory_utilization:.1%}. The number of elements is too large for the allocated memory.",
            "strategy_hint": "DECREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    if scaling_efficiency < 0.5: # Heuristic for "low" efficiency
         return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"Scaling efficiency is low ({scaling_efficiency:.1%}), indicating the number of elements per rank is too small (communication-bound).",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }
    
    if nodes_used == 1 and total_ranks < max_cores_on_node:
        return {
            "decision": "RETRY",
            "reason": f"The node is under-subscribed ({total_ranks}/{max_cores_on_node} tasks used). Hardware is not fully utilized.",
            "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_TASKS",
            "metrics": metrics
        }

    return {
        "decision": "RETRY",
        "reason": f"Performance is at {performance_ratio:.1%} of theoretical max, which is below the {threshold:.1%} threshold. Current configuration is reasonable but can be improved.",
        "strategy_hint": "INCREASE_ELEMENTS",
        "metrics": metrics
    }
